title: Philippine Ecosystems & Climate Change

competencies.text: Describe climate change. Explain biological responses to climate change.
Explain climate change impacts on Philippine ecosystems.

days.title: What Is Climate Change?
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will describe climate change, explain biological responses of organisms to it, and explain its impacts on Philippine ecosystems.

🌦️ Weather vs Climate

Weather is the condition of the atmosphere over hours or days ("It's raining in Iloilo today"). Climate is the average pattern over decades ("The Philippines has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons"). Climate change is a long-term shift in these averages — temperature, rainfall, storms and sea level.

🌍 The Greenhouse Effect

Sunlight warms Earth's surface, which gives off heat (infrared). Greenhouse gases — carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide and water vapor — absorb some of this heat and keep Earth warm enough for life. This natural effect is good.

The problem is the enhanced greenhouse effect: since the 1800s, humans have added large amounts of these gases by:

  • Burning coal, oil and gas for electricity and transport (CO₂)
  • Deforestation, which removes trees that absorb CO₂
  • Livestock, flooded rice fields and landfills (methane)

More heat is trapped, so average temperatures rise — global warming — which then changes rainfall, storms and oceans.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Which statement describes CLIMATE rather than weather?

choices.label: Mindanao gets rain spread through most of the year
It is very cloudy in Baguio this afternoon
A typhoon will hit Samar tomorrow evening
It rained hard in Manila for about two hours today

scenario.explanation: Climate is the long-term pattern of an area. The others describe short-term weather events.

scenario.text: What is the MAIN cause of the recent rise in global temperature?

choices.label: Greenhouse gases from human activities
The Sun moving closer to the Earth
Volcanoes erupting more often each year
The natural greenhouse effect alone

scenario.explanation: Scientific evidence shows that greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels and deforestation are the main driver of recent warming.

scenario.text: Why is the natural greenhouse effect actually helpful?

choices.label: It keeps Earth warm enough for life
It blocks all sunlight from reaching Earth
It removes carbon dioxide from the air
It makes typhoons weaker every year

scenario.explanation: Without any greenhouse gases, Earth's average temperature would be far below freezing.

days.title: How Organisms Respond
days.content:
🐦 Biological Responses

Living things respond to a warming, changing climate in several ways:

ResponseMeaningExample
Range shiftMoving to cooler placesMountain species moving to higher elevations; fish moving to deeper, cooler water
Phenology shiftChanges in the timing of life eventsEarlier flowering; birds nesting or migrating at different times
Behavioral changeChanging activity patternsAnimals more active at night to avoid heat
Coral bleachingStress response to warm waterCorals expel their algae and turn white
Population declineWhen species cannot move or adapt fast enoughMountain-top species with nowhere higher to go

⏳ Why Speed Matters

Evolution usually takes many generations. Today's climate is changing in decades, which is too fast for many species — especially those with small ranges, like many of the Philippines' endemic species found nowhere else on Earth.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its meaning. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Long-term shift in temperature and weather patterns
CO₂, methane and others that trap heat

match.why: It goes beyond the natural effect.

match.right: Change in the timing of life events
Corals expel algae in warm water
match.why: They lose color and may starve.

match.right: Found naturally in only one place

days.title: Impacts on Philippine Ecosystems
days.content:
🇵🇭 Why the Philippines Is Highly Vulnerable

The country is an archipelago with long coastlines, many low-lying cities, about 20 tropical cyclones a year, and communities that depend on fishing and farming. It is also a biodiversity hotspot.

EcosystemImpact
Coral reefs (Tubbataha, Apo Reef)Warm water causes bleaching; ocean acidification (CO₂ dissolving in seawater) weakens coral skeletons; fish catches drop
Mangroves and coastsSea-level rise and storm surges erode coasts; saltwater intrusion affects wells and farms
Forests and mountainsSpecies shift uphill; mountain-top species lose habitat
FarmlandsDroughts during El Niño and floods during strong typhoons reduce rice and corn harvests
CitiesHeat waves; flooding from intense rainfall

🌊 Linked Effects

Impacts chain together: bleached reefs give less shelter to fish, so fishers catch less; weaker reefs also break waves less, so coasts erode faster during storms.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Analyze real impacts and responses. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A diver in Tubbataha Reef finds large areas of white corals after an unusually hot summer. What happened?

choices.label: Warm water made corals expel their algae
Fishermen painted the corals white for tourists
Cold currents froze the top layer of the corals
Sunlight bleached the corals like dry clothes

scenario.explanation: High water temperature stresses corals; they expel the algae that give them color and food, causing bleaching.

scenario.text: A bird that used to nest in lowland forests is now found nesting only at higher elevations. Which response is this?

choices.label: Range shift to cooler areas
Phenology shift in nesting time
Coral bleaching on the mountain
Migration to another country

scenario.explanation: Moving uphill to find cooler conditions is a range shift.

scenario.text: A rice farmer in Nueva Ecija harvests less during strong El Niño years. What is the MOST direct cause?

choices.label: Drought reduces water for the rice fields
Higher CO₂ makes rice plants poisonous
Typhoons always become much weaker in El Niño
Rice grows too fast when the air is warm

scenario.explanation: El Niño often brings below-normal rainfall in the Philippines, and rice needs a lot of water.

scenario.text: Seawater reaches farther inland in a La Union barangay each year during high tide. Which TWO climate factors combine here?

choices.label: Sea-level rise and stronger storm surges
Colder winters and more frequent snow
Lower sea levels and weaker typhoons
More earthquakes and more volcanic eruptions

scenario.explanation: Higher seas and stronger storm surges push saltwater farther onto land.

scenario.text: Why are mountain-top species, like some endemic frogs on Mt. Apo, at special risk?

choices.label: As it warms, they have no higher place to move
They can fly away easily to much cooler countries
Warmer weather gives them more food to eat
Mountains block all greenhouse gases

scenario.explanation: Species already at the summit cannot shift upward any farther, so their suitable habitat shrinks.

days.title: Reading the Evidence
days.content:
📈 Evidence of Climate Change

  • Temperature records: global average temperature has risen about 1.1–1.2 °C since the late 1800s; PAGASA records show warming in the Philippines too.
  • Atmospheric CO₂: measured continuously since 1958 and now far higher than in the past 800,000 years (from ice cores).
  • Sea level: rising as seawater warms and expands and as glaciers and ice sheets melt.
  • Biological signs: more frequent coral bleaching, earlier flowering, species shifting ranges.

🧠 Thinking Critically About Sources

Use reliable sources — PAGASA, DENR, the Climate Change Commission, scientific bodies like the IPCC. Check if a claim is supported by data collected over many years, not one hot day or one cold week. A single weather event is not proof for or against climate change; long-term trends are.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What is the difference between weather and climate?

choices.label: Weather is short-term; climate is the long-term pattern
Weather is long-term; climate is the short-term pattern
They mean exactly the same thing in science today
Weather only refers to rain; climate refers to wind

escape.explanation: Weather describes hours to days; climate describes averages over decades.

escape.text: Which human activity adds the MOST carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?

choices.label: Burning fossil fuels
Planting mangroves
Using solar panels
Recycling plastic bottles

escape.explanation: Coal, oil and natural gas release large amounts of CO₂ when burned for energy and transport.

escape.text: Which is a BIOLOGICAL response to climate change?

choices.label: Fish moving to deeper, cooler waters
Ice sheets melting in Antarctica
Sea levels rising along coastlines
Rainfall patterns shifting in northern Luzon

escape.explanation: A biological response involves living things. The others are physical changes in the climate system.

escape.text: Why does ocean acidification harm coral reefs?

choices.label: Dissolved CO₂ weakens their calcium carbonate skeletons
Acid makes the corals grow far too quickly, so they break
Acid water is too cold for the corals to survive
Acid feeds algae that eat the corals at night

escape.explanation: CO₂ dissolving in seawater forms carbonic acid, making it harder for corals to build their skeletons.

escape.text: A classmate says, "It was cold last night, so climate change isn't real." What is the BEST reply?

choices.label: One night is weather; climate is a long-term trend
Correct — any cold night disproves warming
Correct — climate change only happens in the summer months
Wrong — it is always hot during climate change

escape.explanation: Climate change is measured by long-term averages. A single cold night is normal weather variation.

escape.text: Which Philippine agency provides official weather and climate data?

choices.label: PAGASA
PHIVOLCS
DPWH
DILG

escape.explanation: PAGASA monitors weather and climate; PHIVOLCS handles volcanoes and earthquakes.
